suggestions.title: Train once before Friday — day twelve since your last session, and Friday is where the free part of the layoff ends

rationale.science: A trained lifter loses essentially no strength or size in the first ~2 weeks off, then losses start and run faster inside a calorie deficit — a deficit with no training is the one pairing that spends muscle. (Mujika & Padilla 2000; Bosquet 2013; Garthe 2011)
rationale.data: Last session 8/21 (lower: hack 200, hip thrust 90, extension 160 — left early). Twelve days, zero sessions. Meanwhile the deficit is live: 8/31 logged 2,150 kcal at 20,000 steps.
rationale.relationship: Every day past Friday the layoff stops being free and the deficit starts drawing on lean instead of fat. One logged session — any length — closes the window and gives me the first honest strength read since 8/21. Open every lift at 1–2 reps in reserve; every number is a baseline, not a decline.

suggestions.predict: A session logged by 9/04 with 1–2 RIR openers lands within roughly 5–10% of the 8/21 loads with no hold flags — rust, not loss. No session by 9/04: this card retires and the next brief becomes the comeback plan I promised, framed as baselines.

suggestions.title: Keep logging food forward — one matched day just moved the maintenance math; give it five more

rationale.science: Consistent self-monitoring is the strongest single predictor of fat-loss success; gaps, not metabolism, explain most stalls. (Alhassan 2008; Burke 2011)
rationale.data: 8/31: 2,150 kcal, 175 g protein, 20,000 steps — first food beside a morning weight in eleven days. On that single day the app's maintenance estimate moved 2,429 → 2,353 (range 2,272–2,543, 35 matched days). 9/01 has a weight and no food.
rationale.relationship: The maintenance fit reprices on every matched day. One day makes it jump; five make it settle. The band is the app's call — the only input you control is whether the day exists. A hunch, not a measurement: the estimate keeps wobbling until the window refills.

suggestions.predict: Five of the next seven days logged with food: the maintenance range narrows from ~270 kcal wide and stops moving more than ~50 kcal on any single day. Fewer than three logged by 9/09: this files as a miss on the ask, not on you.

suggestions.title: Tap Approve or Dismiss on one card — nineteen have sat untouched since 8/14 and I can't tell whether that's you or the button

rationale.science: Only graded predictions sharpen a model; an untested proposal teaches nothing either way. This is about the feedback loop, not your body.
rationale.data: Your decision log ends 8/14 (24 entries). Since then nineteen cards went up. You opened the app 8/31 and 9/01 — weight and food landed, the sync carried them — and no card was tapped.
rationale.relationship: A working pipe carried everything except decisions. If the buttons work and you're choosing not to tap, fine — I'll stop counting silence against my record. If they don't work, that's a bug worth one line to the developer. One tap, even Dismiss, answers it. This is a hunch about the app, not a read on you.

suggestions.predict: Any decision dated 9/02 or later appears in the log: the channel works and the freeze was a choice — I stop grading non-decisions. Nothing by 9/05 despite more contact days: I report the button as likely broken and retire this card.
